questions.stem: In Meera's school the girls bring home marks as high as the boys, and in some classes even higher. Yet very few girls from the school go on to higher studies. Explain what stands between the two.

markingPoints.description: Parents prefer to spend resources on their boys' education rather than spending equally on their sons and daughters

The literacy rate among women is only 54 per cent compared with 76 per cent among men, and a smaller proportion of girl students go for higher studies

The result shows elsewhere too: the literacy rate among women is only 54 per cent compared with 76 per cent among men, and a smaller proportion of girl students go for higher studies.

questions.subject: Social Science
questions.stem: Karan's family decides to find out for itself who really does the work at home. Set out the steps Karan should follow to carry out the week's study of activities, and the steps by which he reaches a conclusion about whether women work more than men.

markingPoints.description: Lists all the activities, including household related work, reading and recreation, talking or gossiping, self-care, and taking rest or sleeping
Notes the time taken on each activity by each family member for a week
Adds up the time taken on each activity
Calculates the daily average for each activity for each member and compares the women with the men
Concludes that on an average an Indian woman works one hour more than an average man every day, and that much of this work is not paid and therefore, often not valued

answerScheme.modelAnswer:
Step 1: List every activity - household related activity such as cooking, cleaning, washing, fetching water and looking after children or elders, and also reading and recreation, talking or gossiping, self-care, and taking rest or sleeping. Make new categories if necessary.
Step 2: Note the time taken on each activity by each member of the family for one week.
Step 3: Add up the time taken on each activity, then calculate the daily average for each activity for each member.
Step 4: Compare the totals for the women and the men. On an average an Indian woman works one hour more than an average man every day, yet much of her work is not paid and therefore, often not valued.

questions.stem: A student reads that the country now has only 919 girl children for every thousand boys, and is told that the number is not the same everywhere. Show, step by step, what this ratio counts, what has brought it down, and how the student should use a map of the country to find out more.

markingPoints.description: The child sex ratio is the number of girl children per thousand boys
It has declined in the country to merely 919
Parents prefer to have sons and find ways to have the girl child aborted before she is born
Such sex-selective abortion led to the decline in the child sex ratio
It varies from State to State; identify your own State, compare it with others of a different colour, and find the States which have child sex ratio below 900

answerScheme.modelAnswer:

Step 2: The cause - in many parts of India parents prefer to have sons and find ways to have the girl child aborted before she is born; such sex-selective abortion led to the decline.
Step 3: The pattern - as the map shows, this varies from State to State.
Step 4: Using the map - identify your own State and its child sex ratio, compare it with others shown in a different colour, identify the States which have child sex ratio below 900, and compare the map with the poster.

questions.subject: Social Science
questions.stem: Aaravi's father decides that the cooking, cleaning, washing, fetching of water and the care of the elders are his wife's duty alone, and that her work needs no pay because she stays at home. Aaravi asks you to work out, step by step, what such an arrangement rests on, and why the wife's effort goes unrecorded.

markingPoints.description: The arrangement rests on patriarchy, literally rule by father
Patriarchy is a system that gives men more power over women
So the wife's household work carries no price and is dismissed, and she is called only a housewife
On an average an Indian woman works one hour more than an average man every day
Much of that work is not paid and therefore, often not valued, and the same pattern leads parents to spend on their boys' education rather than on their sons and daughters

answerScheme.modelAnswer:
Step 1: The arrangement rests on patriarchy - literally rule by father.
Step 2: Patriarchy is a system that gives men more power over women, so the wife's household work carries no price and is dismissed as no work at all. That is why she tells outsiders she is only a housewife, even as she works non-stop.
Step 3: She is not idle. On an average an Indian woman works one hour more than an average man every day, and much of her work is not paid and therefore, often not valued.
Step 4: The same pattern runs outside the home - parents prefer to spend their resources for their boys' education rather than spending equally on their sons and daughters, so girls drop out after performing as well as boys.

questions.subject: Social Science
questions.stem:
Kavita's mother is at some task from morning to night. She cooks, cleans, washes, fetches water, looks after the children and the elders, and only sits down when everyone has eaten. When visitors ask her what she does, she says she is only a housewife and does not work. Kavita has begun to add up her mother's hours and is surprised to find that they exceed her father's. She wants to know why so many hours of effort add up to no work at all.

Read the case below and answer the questions that follow. (a) Name the system in which the father rules and men hold more power over women. (b) Why does the mother's long working day add up to no work? (c) Kavita says that work which brings no salary cannot be work. Using the idea of patriarchy, explain why this reasoning is misleading.

answerScheme.modelAnswer: (a) Patriarchy. (b) Much of her work is not paid, and work that is not paid is often not valued; on an average an Indian woman works one hour more than an average man every day. (c) Patriarchy gives men more power over women, so her unpaid household work carries no price and is dismissed, even though she works non-stop.

questions.stem:
Reema and Suresh have worked in the same factory for the same number of hours, doing exactly the same work. At the end of the month Reema's pay packet is the smaller one. Reema knows that a law exists to decide what is due in such a case. At home, her parents never question spending on her brother's schooling, but hesitate when the same sum is needed for her sister. Reema's sister tops the class and yet leaves school after the tenth class.

Read the case below and answer the questions that follow. (a) Name the law and the year that decide what Reema is due. (b) State what the law promises and what Reema actually receives at the factory. (c) Explain why, in Reema's family, a girl who tops the class still leaves school while the family spends on the boy.

(b) It provides that equal wages should be paid to equal work, but women are paid less than men even when both do exactly the same work. (c) Parents prefer to spend their resources on their boys' education rather than spending equally on their sons and daughters, so a smaller proportion of girl students go for higher studies.
